content:
Although Apple's revamped personal assistant is undoubtedly the headline feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate, this year's update includes many other new features and improvements that have nothing to do with Siri AI. Read on as I highlight a few of my favourite new macOS 27 features, or check out the video where I demo each one.

App icon overhaul

macOS 27 has updated virtually every built-in app icon, with some — like Siri, Preview, and Chess — getting thorough redesigns. Other app icons, like Finder, Photos, and Reminders, also received notable updates leaning into the Liquid Glass design language. Very few app icons survived untouched in macOS Golden Gate, although many of the changes are fairly subtle.

If you watch the video below, you'll see a slider comparison view that shows what each app icon looked like in macOS Tahoe, alongside its new design in macOS Golden Gate.

Some of the updates, like the Photos app, I'm a big fan of. Others, like Finder, I'm not entirely sold on. Let me know what you think about the app icon changes in the comments below.

Video: Top macOS 27 features and changes

Comprehensive HDR support

One of the standout features of macOS 27 is its wide-ranging HDR support across the operating system's visuals. Icons, toolbars, and other elements of the Liquid Glass design language gain additional dynamic range support, which users with HDR-capable displays will notice immediately.

To identify which elements have additional dynamic range, you can use the built-in Digital Color Meter utility in macOS to see where shadows or highlights are being clipped when viewing native SDR values. Be sure to watch my video where I explore various areas of the operating system to showcase the HDR support.

If you're using a Studio Display XDR, you've undoubtedly seen the difference already, but even if you haven't picked up Apple's most expensive display, you can still enjoy these benefits on a third-party HDR-capable display.

I recently got hands-on with Asus's ProArt QD-OLED 32-inch 4K display, and the HDR effects in the operating system really pop thanks to the panel tech. Unlike Apple's first-party displays with Extended Dynamic Range support, you'll need to head to Settings > Displays and toggle on the High Dynamic Range switch to take advantage of these benefits.

Recently, I've also started using the Dell UltraSharp U3226Q QD-OLED display, which I'm a huge fan of, and I'll have a review for you soon. On both displays, the HDR elements really stand out — like the blinking cursor in the revamped Spotlight/Siri AI interface.

Design updates

macOS Golden Gate includes a host of design updates in response to criticism of macOS Tahoe. One of my biggest gripes was the inconsistent corner radius across certain windows.

That wasn't the only thing fixed, of course, but it was the most important to me. Other areas that received fixes include floating sidebars, which have returned to edge-to-edge sidebars; the redesigned toolbars with prominent dividers; and the Liquid Glass effect itself has been improved, with a new slider that gives users more control over the balance of translucency and color in the operating system.

Trimmed menus

Another big complaint users had with macOS Tahoe was the unnecessary clutter piled onto menus. In macOS Tahoe, nearly every menu item came with its own little pictogram, making the menus feel chaotic.

If every menu item has an icon, you eventually run out of reasonable icons to use while also diluting the utility of the original pictograms. I'm glad Apple fixed this.

iPhone Mirroring

iPhone Mirroring on macOS 27 gets three major improvements that make it even better on Golden Gate.

  • You can now access Control Center from your mirrored iPhone.
  • You can resize the iPhone Mirroring interface to better match the aspect ratio of an iPad mini.
  • You can play DRM-protected content from your iPhone on your Mac without seeing a black screen.

Without a doubt, iPhone Mirroring gets even more useful in macOS 27!

9to5Mac's Take

While Siri AI is dominating most of the headlines, macOS Golden Gate isn't all about Siri. I've highlighted just a few of my favourite new features here, but there's plenty more to explore. Watch my full video for a walkthrough of all the new features, and let me know your favourites in the comments.
